commit.message:
Stabilize daemon reconnect and Rosetta package startup tests (#55274)

## Why

A replacement daemon PID can appear before the TUI observes the disconnect, allowing stale UI content to make the startup test advance too early. Cold Rosetta translation can also consume the startup deadlines for freshly extracted Intel macOS packages on Apple Silicon.

## What changed

- Wait for the reconnect transcript clear before sending `/status` in the daemon startup test.
- Warm both packaged CLI and app-server entrypoints with `--help` when testing `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages on `arm64` hosts. Give each warmup 180 seconds and fail fixture setup if either entrypoint cannot run.

GitOrigin-RevId: ce75201a7773ebb55cc060ca04b09ec2d0ccf303

Honor per-thread unload delays in app-server (#55270)

## Why

Thread unload timing used the server-wide delay, ignoring per-thread configuration overrides. Clients need to control how long individual idle, unsubscribed threads remain loaded.

## What changed

- Resolve unload timing from each loaded thread's `thread_unload_delay_secs` configuration. Setting it to `0` allows immediate unloading once the thread has no subscribers or activity.
- Allow this runtime retention override in `experimentalPredictionMode` forks while continuing to reject other configuration overrides. Reject negative values and delays too large to schedule.
- Replace the source-specific immediate-unload behavior with explicit configuration.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for per-thread delays, unloading after active turns finish, fork overrides, and invalid prediction-fork delays. Verify that immediate unloading preserves persistent history and that cold resumes and ordinary nested forks use their default delay instead of retaining the previous runtime's override.

GitOrigin-RevId: fcb82bd73a101260c51e2a8476f94320c23ac929

Avoid cloning the full catalog for model metadata lookups (#55265)

## Why

`get_model_info` clones the entire model catalog before selecting metadata for a single model.

## What changed

Look up metadata directly in the active catalog for both remote and static model managers. Share catalog selection across remote catalog accessors and metadata lookup, preserving auth identity checks, API-key discovery policy, provider matching rules, and configuration overrides.

## Testing

Extend coverage for custom catalog configuration overrides, metadata fallback after disabling API-key discovery, and fallback after an auth identity change.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7d0bc4c1ccd2b56e16c7a17c1dbdca05a5c14a7b

Start dormant MCP servers for hook calls (#55263)

## Why

MCP tool hooks need to invoke model-hidden tools even when a subagent's cached server has not started. Their timeout must also cover server startup.

## What changed

- Let cached servers with allowed model-hidden tools remain dormant until called.
- Wait for the selected server when executing an MCP hook, leaving unrelated cached servers dormant, and apply the hook timeout to the entire operation.
- Capture tool namespace attribution after startup and retain it only while catalog revisions remain unchanged.
- Validate the server, environment, and tool filter before starting a server or capturing attribution.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for cached subagent hooks under both startup readiness modes, startup timeouts without context injection, and namespace attribution for hook and token-budget context while keeping tools hidden from the model. Verify that a direct call starts a cached server whose tools are hidden from model exposure.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7a54b69aa2515722aeb925e03e1667bf63aa67ca

Stop memory dual-write when v2 is selected (#55262)

## Why

Dual-write prepares v2 memories while v1 is selected. Once v2 is selected, running the v1 pipeline is no longer needed.

## What changed

Run both memory pipelines only when `memories.dual_write` is enabled and `memories.version` selects v1. Run only v2 when it is selected, even if dual-write remains enabled. Update the configuration documentation and schema to describe this behavior.

## Testing

Extend the startup test to cover both selected versions, checking model request counts, versioned extraction and consolidation state, and the absence of v1 rollout summaries when v2 is selected.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1eb85bd67d7b32883b4ff086514a2acfb6b18f3a

Share dynamic tool specifications across turn snapshots (#55261)

## What changed

Store dynamic tool specifications in an `Arc<[DynamicToolSpec]>` so session configuration and turn snapshots share the list fixed at thread startup instead of copying it on each clone.

Keep the `dynamic_tools()` accessor returning a `Vec<DynamicToolSpec>`, but copy the specifications after releasing the session state lock.

GitOrigin-RevId: 092c5f9ea6cc390d948c27cd11340aeb12bd6037

Unload idle ephemeral composer prediction threads without delay (#55255)

## What changed

Set the app server's unload delay to zero for ephemeral threads whose `thread_source` is `composer_predictions`, excluding subagent sessions. These threads unload once they are idle and have no subscribers, while active turns continue to completion.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage to check immediate unloading after an active prediction turn finishes and after unsubscribing from a fork that inherits the prediction configuration. Verify that persistent threads and ephemeral threads without the prediction source retain the configured delay.

GitOrigin-RevId: 04a0e405b666c689ccf6f482055d24692b18ead0

Preserve rollout access metadata across compression and restoration (#55252)

## Why

Replacing rollout files can lose Unix ownership or macOS ACLs, changing who can read or append to a transcript. An ACL can also permit appending while denying explicit timestamp updates.

## What changed

- Preserve Unix ownership, permissions, modification times, and macOS ACLs before publishing compressed or restored rollouts, and verify the replacement can be reopened.
- Abort replacement on metadata failures, reject macOS delete-deny ACLs to keep temporary files removable, and detect Unix access metadata changes through `ctime` checks.
- Use managed restoration temporary files whose names avoid stale `*.tmp` cleanup.
- Allow appending when refreshing the rollout's modification time returns `PermissionDenied`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for macOS ACL preservation, inherited ACL removal, deletion-protected rollouts, append access despite denied timestamp changes, Unix group preservation, and restoration temporary files surviving stale-file cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: 23f3de6e35c0b2e19f3491170e320159ea3bdb6f

Batch thread history materialization into SQLite (#55244)

## Why

History catch-up collected the entire durable rollout prefix before applying it in one SQLite transaction. Large rollouts therefore required buffering all projection steps and committing them together.

## What changed

Stream projection batches through a bounded queue and commit each batch with its checkpoint. Flush between complete records after reaching 1 MiB of source data or 256 projection steps, keeping ordinal gaps with their following records and allowing oversized records to remain intact.

Wait for batches before opening SQLite transactions so an idle reader does not hold the writer. Preserve committed progress across later failures or cancellation, allowing retries to resume from the last checkpoint.

## Testing

Add coverage for reader and writer failures under backpressure, atomic batch rollback, retries without replaying committed records, and unrelated writes while projection is paused. Verify that producer disconnection and consumer cancellation retain committed progress.

GitOrigin-RevId: 06e79fa4cf273de9abd95faf7eed370f18cedc33

Add Guardian review routing and cached score metrics (#55237)

## What changed

- Count adaptive reviews and record synchronous review routes as `async_fallback` or `required_sync`, with the review reason in snake case.
- Record cached score readiness and score age in milliseconds, measured from input sampling time and including inference time.

## Testing

Extend approval tests to assert fallback routing, adaptive review counts, score readiness, and sampled score age.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1200b3297add6c4467e460de87b4a6d8d31e1fc4

Record Guardian sampling retries, attempts, and delivery outcomes (#55234)

## What changed

- Add sampling retry counters that distinguish transport retries from authentication recovery, with failure reasons.
- Record attempt counts and final outcomes for successful, failed, cancelled, and superseded sampling requests.
- Carry retained-score telemetry until the consumer accepts or discards the score, so queued scores that expire are recorded as superseded and accepted early scores remain successful even if response draining fails.

## Testing

Add metric assertions for transient recovery, retry exhaustion, authentication recovery, cancellation, supersession, and retained-score acceptance or discard, including expiry while a score is queued.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36babd6f431f22cf15b73355e6e026a256a81004

Allow plus signs in metric tags (#55227)

## Why

App versions containing build metadata use `+`, which metric tag validation previously rejected.

## What changed

Accept `+` in metric tag keys and values so these versions can be included in the `app.version` session tag.

## Testing

Extend the session metric tag test to cover a version with build metadata, verifying that its value and tag ordering are preserved.

GitOrigin-RevId: 62ad732b8d280c2d0c4e1b0de8cab26ff87c9d47

Bucket admitted Guardian request metrics by input size (#55226)

## Why

Guardian request counts grouped by input size should reflect admitted sampling inputs without counting synchronous transport retries more than once.

## What changed

- Add a shared `token_bucket` label to admitted total-input observations in `codex.guardian.context.request_tokens` for synchronous and asynchronous reviews. Use inclusive upper bounds in 20k-token steps through 240k, followed by 256k and overflow buckets.
- Record synchronous request tokens after budget admission, once per sampling step, including the complete input. A fresh step counts again even when its input is identical.
- Preserve asynchronous component histograms for oversized classifications, but omit `token_bucket` so rejected inputs do not contribute to counts grouped by that label.

## Testing

Add coverage for bucket boundaries, synchronous retry deduplication and budget rejection, asynchronous retained-history reuse and reset, and admitted versus oversized classification metrics.

GitOrigin-RevId: fac2f102a4c48c5fd21d56bfa701b95a1ff852d0

Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation (#55149)

## What changed

Clean up older standalone releases after verifying the installed command, while holding the install lock. Retain the current and previously selected releases, along with releases used by running Codex processes or bundled helpers.

Record selection history for all standalone installs and preserve it on no-op installs. Only remove validated, installer-owned release directories; skip cleanup when filesystem or process inspection cannot establish that removal is safe. Recheck process usage after moving a release aside and restore it if it is in use.

## Testing

Add installer regression coverage for running helpers, helpers started during cleanup, repeated installs, failed installs, downgrades, and preservation of unowned directories and symlinks.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8fb363750ace14b4f804fdcfcdb210540f49c928

Add observation-only model request lifecycle hooks (#55144)

## What changed

- Add `PreModelRequest` and `PostModelRequest` hooks around model request attempts, including retries. Pass model, session, turn, and optional subagent context; report completion, failure, or cancellation with errors and token usage when available.
- Treat hook output as diagnostic data without allowing it to veto requests or alter model context. Wait for synchronous post-request hooks before dispatching tools, while asynchronous hooks allow streaming tool dispatch to continue.
- Apply memory-consolidation hook filtering and expose the new events through configuration, protocol schemas, generated clients, and the hooks browser.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for failures and retries, ignored control directives, cancellation, synchronous and asynchronous tool ordering, interrupted-turn resume and token accounting, and memory-consolidation filtering. Update hook schema fixtures and hooks browser snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ed7b39fc8bb94cf467e350d07d97fcc729c21ce

Allow agent messages to wake idle root sessions behind a feature flag (#54961)

## Why

A worker can finish after its parent has returned a final answer. Agent messages without `trigger_turn` previously needed an outstanding durable sleep to wake an idle session.

## What changed

Add the disabled-by-default `wake_on_agent_messages` feature to start a new root turn when agent mail arrives through direct delivery or the host mailbox. Reuse the previous turn context for messages without `trigger_turn`. Keep these automatic wakes disabled for interrupted sessions, Plan mode, and child agents.

## Testing

Add coverage for both delivery paths waking a completed root exactly once, child completion waking a parent after its final answer, and the interruption, Plan mode, and child-agent boundaries.

GitOrigin-RevId: f1a4fc7c22be8ca46b2173a85445126cbdd6c4b6

Gate app-server WebSocket compression behind a feature flag (#54949)

## What changed

Add `features.app_server_websocket_compression`, disabled by default. TCP WebSocket and Unix-domain socket listeners now negotiate zstd compression only when the feature is enabled and the client offers the supported protocol. Otherwise, connections use plain text messages.

Include the feature in the configuration schema and allow its override during TUI daemon startup.

## Testing

Extend transport tests to cover enabled and disabled compression with supported, unsupported, and absent client offers on both transports. Add an app-server integration test that verifies startup configuration controls negotiation and the message format used for initialization responses.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6001d65f66f9c48f099b85380c2cad8ffee04de7

Preserve model catalog caches across header credential rotation (#54946)

## Why

Rotating header credentials should not discard the model catalog when a stable account ID is available.

## What changed

- Use the account ID from `CodexAuth::Headers` instead of opaque auth headers in the catalog cache identity. Provider settings remain part of the key.
- Retain credential-sensitive keys when the account ID is missing or the provider uses an explicit API key, bearer token, or command auth.
- Document that hosts using header auth must isolate model managers and cache storage by user and catalog-varying request context, since an account ID can represent a shared workspace.

## Testing

Update the auth-rotation test fixture to omit stable account metadata, preserving coverage for catalog invalidation when opaque credentials change.

GitOrigin-RevId: f96a20c5baf76b9235e131140716731da4dbee81

Share additional tool declarations across response item clones (#54945)

## Why

Cloning `ResponseItem::AdditionalTools` deep-copies its tool declarations for history and request copies.

## What changed

Store `tools` in an `Arc<[serde_json::Value]>` so clones share immutable declarations. Update constructors and existing test fixtures to use the shared representation.

GitOrigin-RevId: eb8831774afb45fe8431a796f34ae9d1243e884a

Add negotiated zstd compression to app-server WebSockets (#54930)

## What changed

- Negotiate compression over TCP and local sockets with `x-codex-app-server-compression: zstd-stream-v1`. Keep JSON text messages when compression is not negotiated.
- Send compressed JSON as binary messages, retaining a separate zstd stream per direction across messages. Export reusable negotiation and codec helpers.
- Limit decompressed messages to 64 MiB and compression windows to 1 MiB. Close compressed connections on decoding errors or unexpected text messages.
- Add audit and deny ignores for the unmaintained `zvariant`, `zbus_names`, and `zvariant_derive` versions pulled in through `zbus`.

## Testing

Add codec tests for retained history, fallback, size limits, malformed data, and oversized compression windows. Add TCP and local-socket round-trip tests covering negotiation, persistent streams, and ping/pong handling, plus TCP fallback for absent or unsupported offers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 50d3861e8fe4a9c523599a5ab773bec7cb883bf2

Support typed content in contextual prompt fragments (#54776)

## Why

Contextual fragments and extension-owned world-state sections currently return strings, limiting them to text content.

## What changed

- Return `ContentItem` from fragment bodies and rendering, preserving classification and attribution. Apply text markers only to `InputText`; pass other content through unchanged.
- Allow extension prompt and world-state contributions to carry typed content, and preserve media in context-window hints.
- Hash non-text world-state fragments by their serialized content and role while retaining the existing text hashing behavior.
- Add shared content-to-tool-output conversion that preserves image references, image detail, and audio.

## Testing

Add coverage for typed world-state hashing and preservation of image content and attribution. Expand code-mode output tests to cover input text, output text, file-backed and inline images, and audio.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2ed00d466a3f169b151202f3eef71e667ea64be1

Defer unknown TUI config fields to the shared strict-config policy (#54766)

## Why

Unknown fields in TUI keymaps and profile TUI settings fail deserialization even when strict config validation is disabled.

## What changed

Remove Serde's `deny_unknown_fields` from these settings so unknown fields are ignored during deserialization and reported by the shared strict-config policy. Keep `schemars(deny_unknown_fields)` so the generated schema continues to disallow unknown fields.

GitOrigin-RevId: 06985161bc3bbb35648712288c1d00bdd50953ba

Stop applying macOS background priority to managed daemons (#54763)

## What changed

Launch managed app-server and updater processes directly through the shared background command helper, removing the macOS `taskpolicy -b` wrapper and its availability probe. Remove the associated launch-policy tests and macOS daemon-startup test serialization.

Retain the 30-second macOS readiness timeout because older updaters can pass background policy to replacement daemons during upgrades.

GitOrigin-RevId: d8620a49139bd2a5c226c624cf7908e06ba7ba38

Upgrade `zip` to 9.0.0 and update plugin archive extraction (#54761)

## Why

Curated plugin archives should preserve executable permissions without applying setuid, setgid, or sticky bits.

## What changed

- Upgrade `zip` from 2.4.2 to 9.0.0, retaining the previous feature set and selecting the existing `bzip2-sys` backend explicitly. Update the Cargo and Bazel lockfiles.
- Adapt plugin extraction to fallible entry names and apply Unix permissions through the open output file, using the mode filtered by `zip`.

## Testing

Add a Unix regression test that encodes special permission bits directly in an archive entry and verifies that the extracted file has mode `0o755`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 75ee6879a372a36b34208c1359f42b670c9d3837

Reduce memory overhead in tool JSON schemas (#54754)

## Why

Schema strings and sequences do not grow after construction, and most schema nodes do not contain maps. Retaining collection capacity and inline optional maps adds unnecessary memory overhead.

## What changed

Store `JsonSchema` strings and sequences as boxed strings and slices, and box optional property and definition maps. Adapt constructors, schema consumers, and existing test expectations to the new representation while preserving the serialized JSON Schema format.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0a249b1ae32932cbbfe3c575c32bfd20b060c303

Render slash command prefixes as composer prompt markers (#54742)

## What changed

- Display the leading `/` in the prompt marker instead of the editable text, sharing prefix state with shell mode's `!`.
- Preserve command prefixes and text element offsets across submission, queuing, history, and external editing. Keep prefixes literal in plain-text composers.
- Track composer-owned slash command elements separately, omit them from exported draft elements, and refresh them when command availability changes.
- Let backward deletion at the start of the text remove the prompt prefix while preserving selected-text deletion and Vim Replace recovery.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for slash prompt cursor placement, prefix deletion, history search highlighting, dynamic command availability, and Vim Replace restoration, including Unicode text. Update rendering snapshots for the slash prompt marker.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0da42da8e98bf7885f9b0ba2c8d5ad4f44d6847e

Gate the file-copy extension behind `multi_env_copy_file` (#54741)

## What changed

Add the `multi_env_copy_file` feature flag, disabled by default and marked as under development, to the feature registry and configuration schema. Install the file-copy extension in app-server threads and CLI debug prompt construction when the flag is enabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6d8b4c7479974f4b70c39f52333491c13d60d2a2

Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)

## Why

Removing a directory while its lock file is open can leave `.nfs*` entries on NFS and prevent cleanup.

## What changed

- Drop the `Arg0PathEntryGuard` lock file before its temporary directory.
- On Unix, rename stale helper directories while locked, then close the lock before deleting them. This prevents initializers from publishing at the old path during cleanup.

## Testing

Extend the guard lifetime test to all platforms and assert that its directory is removed after main returns. Strengthen the janitor test to check that cleanup leaves the temporary root empty.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2524afcc63ed7769a7d16b622c1d447918f9478b

Enable BuildBuddy for voice release builds (#54737)

## What changed

Pass `BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY` to Linux, macOS, and Windows voice release builds, and give the dedicated macOS and Windows voice jobs access to the `bazel` environment without creating deployments.

Use the shared Bazel preparation action and BuildBuddy wrapper for Linux and macOS voice builds so they inherit the existing repository cache and remote cache configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 52cdf05bc4567f3e8c460d2509e57bb30e667868

Preserve prereleased events when creating GitHub prereleases (#54724)

## Why

Publishing a draft prerelease emits a `published` event instead of a `prereleased` event.

## What changed

Create GitHub prereleases with `--draft=false` so they emit `prereleased` events. Keep stable releases as drafts until all asset uploads succeed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 145fd84f852d7ee9cb3c4edff7007a34c3389e1c

Keep prereleases in draft until release assets finish uploading (#54716)

## Why

Prereleases were published before their assets finished uploading, exposing incomplete releases.

## What changed

Create new prereleases as drafts, matching stable releases, and publish them only after all asset uploads succeed. Publishing a draft emits a `published` event rather than a `prereleased` event.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0d1c52038bb9b7beb4b5b9bf52f0ef4c3734de61

Move V8's ICU Bazel rules into the workspace (#54710)

## What changed

Add `third_party/v8/icu.BUILD.bazel` and wire V8's ICU repository to use it instead of patching upstream `bazel/BUILD.icu`.

Select ICU's custom libc++ flags and runtime dependencies through `//third_party/v8:use_rusty_v8_custom_libcxx`, keeping ICU aligned with V8 and its host generators.

GitOrigin-RevId: 92a1b883f5d42d9a3a464002e922295ab166f2bd

Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)

## What changed

Read `desktop.uninstall_codex_home` from the owner's current `config.toml` before recursively deleting a desktop-created Codex home during Windows sandbox uninstall.

- Preserve the home by default for ordinary installations; retain the deletion default for OEM preinstalls when no preference is set.
- Let an explicit boolean preference override either default. Preserve the home when configuration is unreadable, malformed, or contains an invalid preference.
- Capture OEM metadata before Windows removes it during uninstall, and revoke sandbox permissions on retained homes.

## Testing

Add unit tests for missing preferences, explicit overrides, malformed or invalid configuration, and configuration read failures across both installation defaults.

GitOrigin-RevId: 46afc2a7b0f4ecf7f447e46b515e50d0d278e4a8

Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)

## Why

MCP tool discovery discarded response-level `_meta`, leaving server-status clients unable to inspect metadata associated with the tool catalog.

## What changed

- Preserve opaque `_meta` from the first `tools/list` page through catalog refreshes and caches.
- Expose it as `toolListMeta` in `McpServerStatus`, with `null` when unavailable, and update generated schemas and bindings.
- Scope cached Apps catalog metadata to discovery settings, including client capabilities and extensions, while retaining tools from older caches without metadata.
- Restrict server capabilities in status snapshots to the selected servers.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for listing legacy cached Apps tools during failed startup, and update protocol serialization expectations for nullable `toolListMeta`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 62335e2fd8c482067a7a78a7612b58c3eaa9fb55

Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

GitOrigin-RevId: 05a3ca0a901a8dc24337d130548aa2c048b4d586

Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)

## Why

MCP tool calls reported every aborted approval as "user cancelled MCP tool call", including interrupted requests and automatic cancellations in `exec` mode.

## What changed

Carry `user`, `interrupted`, or `non_interactive` cancellation reasons through MCP approval metadata and resolution. Mark explicit TUI cancellations as user actions, interrupted requests as interruptions, and automatic `exec` cancellations as non-interactive.

Use the reason to report when a call was cancelled before approval or because interactive approval is unavailable in `exec` mode. Preserve the existing cancellation message for clients that omit the reason.

## Testing

Update tests to verify that a closed approval response carries the interruption reason and that `exec` cancellation responses include the non-interactive reason.

GitOrigin-RevId: be2a5f7fef539b5db2add53b46aea27e2b8a66fc

Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

## What changed

Add the `codex-multi-env-copy-file` extension, exposing `multi_env_copy_file` when registered by the host. Copy files between distinct selected environments without loading their contents into model context, and return `bytes_copied` on completion.

Require absolute paths in each environment's native path convention and enforce each endpoint's sandbox policy and permission grants. Stream file contents where supported, with a buffered fallback for older executors. Reject same-environment copies and report I/O error kinds without exposing connection details. Warn that failed writes may leave a truncated or partially written target.

## Testing

Add integration tests for binary transfers in both directions, local and remote executors, path validation, opt-in tool visibility, endpoint permissions and grants, and unavailable or disconnected executors. Verify that copied contents stay outside model context.

GitOrigin-RevId: f5d9e423d105019834e0288828cb68c5711b3a49

Use shared Bazel CI preparation for lint and V8 jobs (#54672)

## What changed

- Switch argument-comment lint, rusty-v8 release, and V8 canary jobs to `prepare-bazel-ci` to restore repository caches and configure execution logs. Use `bazel-argument-comment-lint` and `bazel-v8` cache scopes.
- Include changes to `prepare-bazel-ci` in V8 canary path detection.
- Pass `BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY` to the `MODULE.bazel.lock` check.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ef150f93413d1d30287f0728358eed26e792204

Distinguish retryable thread-store errors from unknown write outcomes (#54664)

## What changed

Add `ThreadStoreError::Retryable` for transient failures known to be safe to retry and `ThreadStoreError::OutcomeUnknown` for writes that may already have committed. Recovery remains the operation owner's responsibility; neither category automatically triggers retries.

Preserve existing app-server error mappings and fatal session startup behavior, and report the new categories in shutdown diagnostics without exposing raw error payloads.

## Testing

Add coverage for conservative SQLx error classification, mutation error mappings, session initialization categories, and shutdown diagnostics that omit raw error payloads.

GitOrigin-RevId: 259a9bfaa6ff3cbfa2ee61a01a1f1e744c90f118

Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)

## Why

MCP servers can expose new tools during discovery. Refreshing the catalog after a tool-list notification lets Codex discover and call those tools in the same turn.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for ordinary MCP servers.
- Track notifications in transport order and refresh catalogs before subsequent discovery or tool binding. Coalesce concurrent refreshes and retry listings invalidated by notifications, including during pagination.
- Retain the previous catalog on refresh failure, apply a retry cooldown, and invalidate affected startup caches. Allow notification refreshes to proceed while admitted calls finish.

## Testing

Add coverage for same-turn discovery and invocation in direct and Code Mode, notifications during startup and pagination, disabled behavior, cache invalidation, and concurrent refreshes with timeout recovery.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9afee8deba00dd9851b5f32625f61f96965aa00c

Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)

## Why

Dynamic tool calls should remain independent while waiting for client responses, so one pending call does not block another from reaching the client.

## What changed

Enable parallel execution in `DynamicToolHandler`, allowing code mode programs to issue concurrent dynamic tool calls with `Promise.all`.

## Testing

Add a code mode regression test that waits for two dynamic tool requests before responding, resolves them in reverse order, and verifies that `Promise.all` preserves the expected result order.

GitOrigin-RevId: c93c1fea720f76c772b0e3452ddc8c01fb1a08d8

Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)

## Why

Authorization server metadata can advertise scopes unrelated to the MCP resource. Using that list for discovery can request broader scopes than the resource requires.

## What changed

Update `rmcp` and use its initial scope selection during OAuth discovery: prefer scopes from the initial `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, fall back to protected resource metadata, and include `offline_access` when supported. Stop using the authorization server's general scope list as the discovered resource scopes.

## Testing

Add coverage for challenge scope precedence, resource metadata fallback, scope normalization, and exclusion of unrelated authorization server scopes. Add a no-browser login regression test for a preregistered client whose authorization server advertises neither scopes nor dynamic registration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68d83cf61fb0b73dac9e861e476f484990fd93b6

Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

## What changed

Wait for the rejected socket to close before advancing Tokio's clock through
capped retry delays. Keep socket I/O on real time so pending handshakes cannot
auto-advance their own timeouts.

Return bodyless HTTP 409 responses in the test server, check that neither
rejection restarts fast retries, and assert that recovery preserves the expected
reconnect attempt count. Both cursor and cursorless cases use the updated helper.

GitOrigin-RevId: da167312f28b7e24b864e6929be749865ea70081

Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)

## What changed

- Attempt each `npm publish` up to three times, with 10- and 20-second delays and fresh OIDC credentials on each attempt. Continue skipping already-published versions.
- Enable verbose npm logging and retain debug logs as artifacts for seven days, including on failure.

Add macOS coverage for metadata and workspace-root case aliases, explicit grants, narrower restrictions, and missing directories. Strengthen the patch regression test to assert the approval rejection message for both direct `apply_patch` calls and shell interception.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8ae2eb97ce6ec71c51bead130515b9ce6c1cdfab

Add regression coverage for Guardian sandbox retry approvals (#54265)

## What changed

Add an integration test that approves a sandboxed `exec_command` attempt, simulates a sandbox denial, and denies the subsequent unsandboxed retry. Verify that Guardian reviews the retry separately with `require_escalated`, that the denied retry never reaches the executor, and that the tool result includes the denial rationale.

Use a fake executor to exercise the sandbox denial consistently across hosts.

GitOrigin-RevId: cd644255f7a7b7561c9e52a5b6e40f0859b70547

Track Guardian transcript admission across failed reviews (#54264)

## Why

A failed Guardian inference can retain its input in a reusable session. Tracking transcript progress only after successful reviews can admit the same evidence again on retry.

## What changed

Advance transcript progress when a failed turn has retained its input and the session remains reusable, without counting it as a completed review or changing the committed fork checkpoint. Leave progress unchanged when failure occurs before input admission.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for encrypted agent messages across review retries, pending evidence after compaction failures, and fork checkpoints after transcript admission without a completed review.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36239ec9d47f484bcfe68d65e7c8d8ab8660db0d

Require fresh Guardian approval for escalated tool retries (#54263)

## Why

Guardian approval covers the permissions of the reviewed action. A retry outside the sandbox needs a fresh review of its broader permissions.

## What changed

- Track the initial approval source so Guardian approval does not preapprove an escalated retry, while preserving existing user and hook approval behavior.
- For exec retries that can run without the sandbox, set the approval action to `RequireEscalated` and clear `additional_permissions` so review and caching reflect the retry's actual permissions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 06f8d53745a7bcfe9fdb5628ff9e85da6060547d

Preserve recent speech when trimming realtime transcripts (#54257)

## Why

Trimming interleaved realtime transcripts by utterance order can discard the latest speech from an earlier utterance. Evicting after each delta can also drop one speaker before the other speaker's delta from the same frame arrives, losing recent instructions at handoff.

## What changed

Use raw frame recency to trim timed frameless bidirectional transcripts within the 8 KiB budget. Defer eviction until the frame advances or the transcript is consumed, and retain both speakers' suffixes when they share the newest frame. Preserve conversation order and fall back to FIFO eviction when timing is unavailable.

Track trimmed prefixes so final transcripts can extend retained speech without making delayed finals appear newer.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for frame recency, same-frame event ordering, UTF-8 truncation, delayed finals, and untimed fallback. Add an app-server handoff test verifying that both speakers' recent speech and the latest user instruction survive while live transcript notifications remain unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: b01b729d8bdd4acb26e0385442ce40819355deac

Add regression tests for case-variant metadata protection (#54250)

## What changed

- Verify that freeform `apply_patch` calls and shell-intercepted patches cannot modify `.git/config` through `.GIT/config` when approvals are disabled, while an ordinary workspace file remains writable.
- Add macOS Seatbelt coverage for uppercase protected metadata paths, including absent directories, existing directories with either casing, and case variants of the workspace root. Assert that metadata creation and modification are denied while sibling workspace writes succeed.

The tests skip filesystems that do not support the case-insensitive aliases they exercise.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5cf6b0c36eee348e1ba0db0bc2d3bff072458364

Apply syntax theme colors to Markdown prose in the TUI (#54217)

Use the active syntax theme's markup foregrounds for headings, emphasis, strong text, list markers, links, and blockquotes. Preserve existing bold, italic, and underline modifiers, and retain previous styles when a scope provides no foreground.

## Testing

Update rendering snapshots and streaming blockquote assertions for themed colors. Exercise existing fallback expectations with an empty syntax theme.

GitOrigin-RevId: b00aa4af30f73f538ff5f888a0f9b4edbdc15893

Show image previews in the fullscreen transcript (#54216)

## What changed

Render local viewed images and generated image artifacts as bounded thumbnails in the rich fullscreen transcript using Kitty or Sixel graphics. Viewed images appear when their activity is expanded or the detailed presentation is active; generated images appear alongside their saved-path entry.

Keep previews clipped to the viewport, retain graphics across unrelated redraws, and remove them when overlays open. Bound image decoding and cache memory, and preserve text-only entries for remote workspaces, unsupported terminals, missing files, and oversized images. Image rows do not enter searchable or selectable text.

## Testing

Add layout and snapshot coverage for disclosure, viewport clipping, rewrapping, raw-mode fallback, deleted files, and oversized rasters. Add terminal coverage for retained Kitty graphics, repainting after a clear, local-file transport, and overlay cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: fb2ec146331acfcfc82b2b283616671c9ee93757

Retire worktree and voice feature flags (#54175)

## What changed

- Remove feature-flag checks from managed worktree creation and repository-aware session discovery, while retaining local workspace and trust checks.
- Make TUI voice availability follow platform support instead of `features.realtime_conversation`.
- Ignore `features.worktrees` and `features.realtime_conversation` configuration overrides, warn when managed requirements reference them, and hide both flags from `/experimental`, including catalogs from older servers.

## Testing

Add coverage for ignored configuration overrides and managed requirements, and update session filtering, worktree grouping, and experimental feature discovery tests for the retired flags.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1d64e890e6e2f8a78926a9ea163126c0890b068e

Preserve ChatGPT authentication for Gov MCP servers (#54170)

## Why

MCP servers at `https://gov.chatgpt.com` were treated as untrusted for ChatGPT authentication and switched to OAuth, preventing local Gov Apps from retaining the ChatGPT auth provider.

## What changed

Trust the `https://gov.chatgpt.com` origin alongside the existing ChatGPT origin when resolving MCP server authentication. Origin matching preserves scheme, host, and port restrictions.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for Gov Apps URL construction, trusted origin normalization, rejection of lookalike hosts and nonstandard schemes or ports, and retention of the local ChatGPT auth provider. Verify that explicit OAuth servers and servers in remote environments do not receive the host provider.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7ceaf7c524d963005d9f23204489bbde269f0dd5

Reload the model catalog after account changes (#54169)

## Why

The app server retained its startup model provider for catalog requests, so signing in or out could leave `model/list` using stale provider settings or requiring a restart after managed provider requirements changed.

## What changed

- Invalidate the catalog after successful login and logout, then reload the effective configuration on the next model list or background refresh. Rebuild the models manager when the provider or catalog changes, while preserving existing threads' routes.
- Retain the original project context and the TUI's `--oss` provider selection across reloads. Retry configuration loading after falling back to defaults so temporary failures do not pin the fallback catalog.
- Keep provider policy checks for cached catalogs and apply runtime `api_key_model_discovery` toggles to the active catalog manager.

## Testing

Add and extend tests for provider selection and definition changes after login, catalog reloads after logout, OAuth gateway transitions, fallback recovery, project context, and runtime model discovery toggles.

GitOrigin-RevId: bce2e23ff567e1a52eac2b6ad736a6e63ff61e2b

Generate keymap descriptors and binding accessors from one catalog (#54151)

## Why

The `/keymap` action catalog and root-config binding lookup duplicated the same action inventory, requiring both to be maintained together.

## What changed

Use `define_keymap_actions!` to generate `KEYMAP_ACTIONS` and `binding_slot` from a single declaration grouped by context. Preserve the existing action order, descriptions, feature gates, and binding mappings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 182e937d9642a8b5a4aa787691da793712f29010

Allow large file writes over direct exec-server WebSockets (#54135)

## Why

Direct mode serves executor requests but applied the client's 8 KiB inbound request limit, causing larger `fs/writeFile` requests to disconnect the executor.

## What changed

Use a dedicated direct WebSocket connection constructor that omits the client inbound request limit while retaining WebSocket message and frame limits.

## Testing

Add a regression test that runs the direct environment and verifies successful file writes above the client request limit using both text and binary WebSocket messages.

GitOrigin-RevId: e8e77a5e8581ab9eb98446e23b77a6da41d64868

Record per-tool incremental update and description size metrics (#54133)

## What changed

Tag `codex.tools.incremental_updates` counters with the qualified tool name alongside the action. Continue excluding initial catalogs and namespace headers, while counting each removed namespace member.

Add `codex.tools.spec_description_bytes` to measure UTF-8 description bytes when an existing tool definition is replaced. Skip definitions without descriptions and use logarithmic histogram boundaries up to 1 MiB.

## Testing

Extend namespace transition tests to check per-tool counts and description sizes. Add scenario assertions for replacement metrics with incremental tool updates and their absence on the non-incremental request path.

GitOrigin-RevId: e20e6d81f21a867b285df1f0da005c2806dd03c6

Allow stdin review under active grants with sandbox prompts disabled (#54119)

## Why

With granular sandbox approvals disabled, `write_stdin` rejected input to terminals retaining additional permissions even when those permissions were still granted.

## What changed

Let input reach approval review when the terminal's retained permissions match active grants for its environment. Require identical filesystem grants, including entry order, and an active network grant when retained permissions enable network access. Each input still requires review.

Keep rejecting input when retained authority is no longer covered or the approval policy changes to `Never`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for user and Guardian review, turn grant expiry, session grants, and switching to `Never`. Cover filesystem restrictions, protected metadata, symlinks, and ordered denials, and verify that rejected input never reaches the terminal.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9abf7da8d03b1526d26ca2a718e36349a255330b

Report terminal completion states and blocking reasons (#54114)

## Why

Terminal status previously collapsed completed and failed turns into `idle` and reported blocking prompts without a reason. Blocking detection also depended on terminal title settings.

## What changed

- Emit `done` and `error` through OSC 7501 for live turn results, retaining them until deliberate keyboard, paste, or mouse input acknowledges them. Mouse movement does not acknowledge results.
- Classify blocking requests with `kind=permission`, `kind=question`, or `kind=auth`, including requests hidden behind another view or delayed while typing, independently of terminal title settings.
- Keep pending follow-up work and active goals `working`. Treat interrupted turns and replayed results as `idle` rather than new results.
- Preserve the existing iTerm2 OSC 21337 labels and indicators, mapping `done` and `error` to `Idle`.

## Testing

Add lifecycle and input-acknowledgment tests covering approvals, completion, failure, interruption, replay, pending follow-ups, and active goals. Extend blocking-request assertions and terminal protocol snapshots for the new states and reasons.
